title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools

summary: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks continue processing from where they left off once the update completes. This capability is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is supported. To learn more, visit Amazon MSK Connect developer guide .

summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can select cryptographic groups from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our getting started page .

summary: Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle now support RDS storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes . RDS storage autoscaling automatically scales storage capacity in response to growing database workloads, with zero downtime. Additional storage volumes allow you to add up to three additional volumes to increase your storage capacity up to 256 TiB. Previously, you had to manually provision storage capacity on the additional storage volumes based on anticipated application capacity demands while autoscaling could be enabled on the primary storage volume. Under-provisioning could result in application downtime, and over-provisioning could result in under-utilized resources and higher costs. With RDS storage autoscaling, you simply set your desired maximum storage limit for each additional storage volume, and autoscaling takes care of the rest. RDS storage autoscaling continuously monitors actual storage consumption, and scales capacity up automatically when actual utilization approaches provisioned storage capacity. Autoscaling works with new and existing database instances. Autoscaling has no additional charges and you only pay for the provisioned storage resources. You can enable it by using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or Amazon RDS API. RDS storage autoscaling for additional storage volumes is available for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Amazon RDS for Oracle in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account. From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. Partners can revoke a subsidiary authorization or a subsidiary connection at any time, which immediately stops that subsidiary from creating new offers — agreements and offers already extended to buyers remain unchanged. This capability is available today at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, see Managing subsidiary account connections and Creating private offers as a subsidiary account .
title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts

summary: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use. With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise be more capacity than a single model needs. You configure GPU partitioning when you create an endpoint that hosts inference components, and you continue to invoke each model by name, so your application code doesn't change. GPU partitioning is available on P4d, P5, G7, and G7e instances in US East (N. title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints

summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog. Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs. You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see Supported Regions for table optimizers . To learn more, see Optimizing Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Developer Guide. To get started, visit the AWS Glue product page .
title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region

summary: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch . The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters. Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus and Amazon CloudWatch .
title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics

summary: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version. Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see Flow versioning and aliasing in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the Amazon Connect Customer website.
title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows

The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP). Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distribution removes that per-application work. Automatic SDK integration is available for web ACLs that are used with Amazon CloudFront and contain at least one of those managed rule groups. You can configure it using the AWS Management Console, CLI, SDK, CDK, or CloudFormation. In the AWS WAF console, the setting appears with the managed rule group settings and is on by default for new web ACLs that you create with one of those rule group. summary: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now lets you turn off automatic minor version upgrades on new and existing DB instances that use the JVM, Spatial, Locator, or OLAP option. Previously, these options required automatic minor version upgrades to be enabled. With this change, you decide when to apply minor version upgrades to DB instances using these options. If you turn off automatic minor version upgrades, we recommend that you apply new minor versions regularly so your DB instances keep the latest Oracle security fixes. To keep automatic minor version upgrades turned on and still control the order in which your environments are upgraded, you can use AWS Organizations upgrade rollout policy . This change is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more about options available in Amazon RDS for Oracle, see Adding options to Oracle DB instances in the Amazon RDS User Guide.
title: Amazon RDS for Oracle no longer requires automatic minor version upgrades for JVM, Spatial, Locator, and OLAP options

summary: Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later. Customers can opt in to TLS 1.3 by selecting a named security policy in their MSK cluster configuration, with no change to existing clusters until a policy is applied. A named security policy defines which TLS version and cipher suites a cluster can accept. With this launch, Amazon MSK provides a set of policies customers can select and any connection that does not meet the selected policy requirements is rejected. This allows customers to stay in control of their security and compliance posture. Policies that support both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 allow connections to negotiate the highest version the client supports allowing clients that support TLS 1.3 to connect on it immediately while clients on TLS 1.2 continue to connect on TLS 1.2. This lets customers upgrade their clients at their pace before applying a stricter policy. title: Amazon MSK now supports TLS 1.3 for data in transit

summary: Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC). With CloudFront-Viewer-ISP, you can break down traffic and performance by network. You can also isolate unusual traffic from a single provider. CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details includes the key exchange, signature scheme, and signature public key type for each connection. You can use it to measure the share of viewers that actually connect with PQC and identify clients that do not yet do so. To forward either header to your origin, add it to an origin request policy and attach the policy to your distribution. To get started, see adding CloudFront headers and controlling origin requests with a policy in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide
title: Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details

summary: Security teams need powerful tools to find vulnerabilities, test exploits, and build defenses. Daybreak Red from OpenAI is now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East), bringing advanced AI to this work. Part of OpenAI’s Daybreak cyber defense initiative, Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber is built for authorized vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. It gives verified defenders more room to investigate complex security problems, with fewer refusals for this work and stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls. Daybreak Red runs on Bedrock’s next-generation inference engine, with zero-operator access enforced at the chip. Your inference data is not used to train models, and you do not need to share your Daybreak Red data with OpenAI. The model is available in US East (Ohio) and AWS GovCloud (US-East). Access to the model requires enrollment in Daybreak access from OpenAI. To get started, contact OpenAI or your AWS account team about Daybreak eligibility. Once approved, work with your AWS account team to enable access. Learn more in the blog .
title: Daybreak Red from OpenAI now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East)

When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.
title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts

summary: Kiro web search gives the agent real-time access to current information on the internet, so its answers draw on up-to-date search results and page content. The agent uses web search automatically when a question involves recent changes or topics beyond the model's training data. Answers that use web results include citations. Kiro enterprise administrators can turn off web search and web fetch for their organization from the Kiro console under Settings. Teams can also remove web tools from individual custom agents, or block them with capability-based permission rules. For more details, visit the AWS GovCloud (US) documentation , the monitoring and tracking guide , or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page .
title: Web Search now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)

summary: Amazon Quick introduces Quick Essentials for enterprises. The plan makes it easier for organizations to get started with all the features of Quick such as AI-powered chat, Research, Flows, and Apps, and lets users view and interact with Quick Sight dashboards and reports and then manage adoption at the desired pace. In AWS Regions where Amazon Quick is available, Quick Sight Reader users are upgraded to Quick Essentials at no additional per-user cost. With Quick Essentials, Quick Sight Readers can ask their dashboards questions in plain language, like what drove a revenue dip in March, and dig into the details with follow-up questions. They can turn the answer into a document, presentation, or spreadsheet for their team. When they need more context, Research pulls from their data, files, and the web into a detailed report with citations. If they need the same update every week, Flows can build it and send it automatically. When they need a tool that doesn't exist yet, like a request tracker, they can describe it and Apps builds it, without writing code. Existing dashboards, Favorites, and Recents stay in place. Row-level and column-level security apply to every answer, and data is not shared across customers or used to train shared models. Administrators continue to manage the capabilities with custom permission profiles that can be applied to any user or a role. title: Amazon Quick Introduces Quick Essentials

summary: Amazon Connect Customer Outbound Campaigns now provides flow designer analytics for journeys, so you can see directly on a journey flow how many customers reached each step and which branch they took. A journey is a multi-step outbound campaign that reaches your customers by voice, email, SMS, or WhatsApp, and branches based on customer behavior. Campaign managers can use these metrics to find the steps in a journey that need changes. A collections team running a payment reminder journey can see how many customers moved from the first SMS reminder to a follow-up call. If the SMS step shows a high error rate, the team can add an email step to its error branch so future customers on that path still get a reminder. You can use flow designer analytics for journeys in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Monitor flow performance with metrics in flow designer analytics mode in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide .
title: Amazon Connect Customer Outbound Campaigns now provides journey analytics
